title: Incremental Schema Checkpointing and Deterministic Tool-Invoke Acceptance
creator: Elena Park
description: Define acceptance criteria, test cases, and rollout guardrails for a new Incremental Schema Checkpointing protocol plus a deterministic, replay-safe function/tool invocation model for streamed and non-streamed responses. This ticket clarifies scope changes to existing structured-output work: adds numbered checkpoints, resume tokens, idempotency token surface, and a deterministic replay matrix for integrations (hosted/Dedicated/Private).
acceptance_criteria: Schema checkpoint envelope is defined: every emitted structured fragment MUST include a monotonic checkpoint_id (string) and optional resume_token (opaque string) when the response is resumable.
Server and client agree on a minimal 'anchor' schema: anchor_schema_version field included in the first checkpoint; mismatch results in documented soft-fail fallback (see fallback modes).

Tool/function invocation contract: every outbound invocation from the runtime includes an invocation_id (UUID), caller_id (route id), and idempotency_key. Invocations MUST be replay-safe up to the idempotency window documented in runtime-1.21.

Idempotency semantics matrix implemented and validated: at-most-once (default), at-least-once (opt-in), and exactly-once approximation (best-effort with deduplication map). Tests must prove each behavior across failures.

Streaming backpressure behavior defined: if the client signals stop/resume via resume_token policy, runtime pauses emission and persists latest checkpoint to durable store within 200ms SLO for Dedicated and 500ms for hosted. Failure to persist triggers documented rollback path.

Partial-object reconciliation: when a resumed stream emits overlapping fragments the SDK must reconcile by checkpoint_id and sequence offsets; server emits a reconciliation patch frame when overlap detected.

Observability and telemetry: each checkpoint emission logs telemetry with fields [route, model, checkpoint_id, resume_token_present, invocation_id, latency_ms, checkpoint_size_tokens]. These events are recorded at 100% sampling for internal rollout and 1% thereafter.

API/SDK compatibility: SDKs (python/js/go) provide a stable resume() helper that accepts resume_token and returns an idempotent stream handle; tests verify identical JSON envelope ordering between fresh and resumed sessions for deterministic workloads.

Fault injection tests: with simulated transient failures (network drop, process restart), at least 95% of resume attempts result in correct reconstituted structured output without duplicate tool side-effects for standard idempotent endpoints.
Security and privacy: resume_token does not leak sensitive PII; tokens are bound to a route and TTL-limited. Security review sign-off required before rollout to customer-facing buckets.
success_metrics: Resume success rate >= 99% for internal deterministic test corpus across hosted and Dedicated runs
Tool-invoke duplicate side-effect rate < 0.1% under randomized replay tests
Mean checkpoint persistence latency < 120ms for Dedicated in production-like load
No increase in SLO violations for normal non-resume traffic post-rollout (within 1 percentage point)
test_cases: TC-01: Fresh full-stream generation produces ordered checkpoint envelopes with incremental checkpoint_id values and anchor_schema_version on first checkpoint.
TC-02: Simulate client disconnect after checkpoint N, resume using resume_token -> verify output from checkpoint N+1 and no duplicate tool invocations (idempotency_key honored).
TC-03: Replay invocation with same invocation_id but different payload -> verify deduplication map prevents duplicate side-effects and logs a conflict telemetry event.
TC-04: Downgrade client to mismatched anchor_schema_version -> verify server emits 'schema_mismatch' envelope and graceful fallback mode (best-effort-json) documented in API error code 409-SCHEMA.
TC-05: Backpressure test: client sends pause signal mid-checkpoint; verify runtime persists checkpoint to durable store and resumes correctly within defined SLOs.
TC-06: Security test: resume_token replay across different route/tenant -> token rejection and audit log entry generated.
TC-07: Performance test: emit 10k small checkpoints across models and ensure telemetry scales and persistence latency targets met.
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start in internal-only bucket for 2 weeks with synthetic workloads
Enable for Beta customers (opt-in) for 4 weeks, collect telemetry and run dedicated e2e scripts
Gradual 25/50/100% expansion with monitoring alerts and automated rollback if duplicate-invoke rate > 0.2%
Final GA after security review and docs publication
rollback_criteria: Duplicate tool-invoke side-effect rate > 0.2% for a rolling 1h window
Resume success rate < 95% for Beta customers after 48h
Unresolved security review findings classified as 'blocker'
Unexpected >2 percentage point increase in latency SLO violations for baseline traffic
notes: Scope change: adds persistent checkpoint store and new idempotency headers on invocations; ENG scope increased to include durable-store adapters for Dedicated and hosted.
Compatibility note: Private customers can opt out of resume persistence and rely on local in-memory resume if they cannot permit durable-store usage; document trade-offs.
Design alternative considered: vector-clock style non-monotonic fragment IDs was rejected in favor of monotonic checkpoint_id to simplify reconciliation across heterogeneous clients.
